task.description: Step 2 of WF-03 for ISS-0421 (narrowed scope per Step 1): design a fix bounding the 7 sweeps' serial per-tenant iteration in lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex's handle_info(:tick, state) using Task.async_stream (or equivalent), without exceeding Repo pool_size(10) and without a second tenant_schemas/0 query per tick. No supervision-tree changes (REQ-219/ISS-0451 already own that ground).

result.summary:
Wrote lib/letflow/design/iss0421-poller-bounded-concurrency.md. Confirmed pool_size: 10 is current in config/dev.exs and config/runtime.exs (config/test.exs uses a different, test-only sizing per ISS-0194/decision 0009, irrelevant here). Confirmed Letflow.Admission.init/1 already derives global_cap = pool_size(10) - reserved_headroom(2) = 8, a PLATFORM-WIDE, non-blocking counting-semaphore budget shared with HTTP (lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex, REQ-217) and already consumed by 6 of the Poller's 7 sweeps via with_admission/3 (every sweep except maybe_refresh_active_instances/1, which REQ-218's own moduledoc records as DELIBERATELY left unwrapped).

Key design decision, load-bearing for the whole doc: since 6 of 7 sweeps already route every per-tenant call through Admission.try_acquire(:global), Admission.global_cap (8) is ALREADY the true ceiling on concurrent DBConnection checkouts for those 6 sweeps, independent of whatever Task.async_stream max_concurrency this design picks -- a 9th concurrent attempt gets {:error, :capacity} and skips (existing, unchanged behavior). So max_concurrency: 8 for those 6 sweeps is the number that lets every admittable task get spawned with zero tasks spawned that are certain to lose the admission race. The 7th sweep (maybe_refresh_active_instances/1) has NO admission backstop, so its bound must be justified directly against pool_size: chose max_concurrency: 2, exactly matching Admission's own reserved_headroom, so the worst-case platform-wide peak during that sweep's window (8 concurrent HTTP admission grants + this sweep's own 2) is exactly 8+2=10=pool_size, never exceeded -- matching SandboxPool moduledoc's own no-hand-waving arithmetic standard.

Sweep ordering: kept strictly SEQUENTIAL relative to each other (only per-tenant iteration WITHIN one sweep becomes concurrent) -- rejected letting 2+ sweeps run concurrently with each other because the 6 Admission-gated sweeps share one global_cap(8) budget, and concurrent sweeps would cause them to silently cannibalize each other's admission grants tick over tick (a correctness regression, not just a safety one), and because the maybe_refresh_active_instances/1 arithmetic assumes it never overlaps another Poller sweep's own peak.

Fault isolation (AC1): Task.async_stream/3 options specified precisely -- on_timeout: :kill_task (required; default :exit would crash the whole Poller GenServer on one tenant's timeout, the opposite of AC1), a new timeout: value via a new Letflow.Scheduler.sweep_task_timeout_ms/0 accessor (default 10_000ms, following the exact existing poll_interval_ms/0 config-read-fresh pattern -- flagged as an open question against poll_interval_ms's shorter 5_000ms default, recommendation given not silently assumed), and zip_input_on_exit: true for per-tenant log tagging. Separately, and required IN ADDITION to on_timeout, a per-task top-level rescue is specified for the 2 call sites lacking one today (poll-and-fire loop, retention sweep) because Task.async_stream's default raise behavior terminates the WHOLE stream/caller, a strictly larger blast radius than Enum.each's ever was -- the other 4 sweeps already have an inline try/rescue and need no second one.

AC4 (single tenant_schemas/0 query/tick): explicitly confirmed unaffected -- fetch_tenant_schemas/0's one call site and the schemas list threaded to all 7 sweeps by reference are both untouched; converting a sweep's traversal from Enum.each to Task.async_stream does not change how many times its caller computes schemas.

Interaction with REQ-219/ISS-0451: addressed explicitly as orthogonal -- this design's per-task rescue and on_timeout:kill_task mean a persistent per-tenant fault (the exact case those two mechanisms exist for) is now caught INSIDE the task and no longer reaches handle_info/2 as an unhandled raise, reducing how often the Pollers restart-intensity override / PollersBreaker are exercised for that fault class, but does not make either redundant -- any OTHER cause of the Poller process itself crashing (including the untouched forced-crash test seam) still hits that machinery exactly as today. No changes made or needed to lib/letflow/supervisor/* or application.ex.

Per-sweep judgment (not blanket treatment): all 7 sweeps get Task.async_stream (all 7 have the identical Enum.each-over-schemas-doing-per-tenant-DB-work shape, so none qualify as 'too light to bother'), but split into 2 differently-justified bound classes (8 vs 2) rather than one number applied uniformly -- the real differentiator found was Admission-wrapped vs. not, not sweep 'weight'.

Open questions flagged, not silently resolved: (1) sweep_task_timeout_ms default (10s) vs poll_interval_ms default (5s) ordering; (2) reserved_headroom(2) being a single shared allowance with no current inventory of every non-admission-gated Repo consumer drawing on it, of which this design's maybe_refresh_active_instances/1 bound is now one identified consumer; (3) whether a named Task.Supervisor (SandboxPool precedent) is needed here -- design argues no (no async-orphan risk, calling process already blocks until the stream drains) but flags it for REVIEWER confirmation rather than assuming it.

No implementation code in the design doc -- prose, arithmetic, and named config-accessor descriptions only, no defmodule/def/do-block code.
result.routing: Route to Step 2b CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR to gate lib/letflow/design/iss0421-poller-bounded-concurrency.md. Pay particular attention to: (1) the 8-vs-2 max_concurrency arithmetic in the design's section 3 (both the Admission.global_cap reasoning for the 6 gated sweeps and the reserved_headroom-exact-match reasoning for maybe_refresh_active_instances/1); (2) whether the fault-isolation mechanism in section 4 (on_timeout: :kill_task + explicit per-task rescue) actually achieves AC1's 'one slow/erroring tenant doesn't block others' property as claimed; (3) the 3 open questions in section 8 -- confirm they are genuinely open rather than things the design should have resolved itself.
